title: whPRP Security of SPACE256-16
summary: At concrete leakage, time, query, and advantage bounds, SPACE256-16 is conjectured to be whPRP-secure; proving or refuting the claim remains open.

formal_statement.body: Prove or refute the conjecture that $\mathrm{SPACE256\text{-}16}$, the 256-bit-block variant of $\mathrm{SPACE\text{-}16}$, is a $(\lambda,t,q,t_{\mathrm{lif}},q_{\mathrm{sim}},\varepsilon)$-secure $\mathrm{whPRP}$ for leakage $\lambda\approx 2^{20}$ bits, adversarial running time $t\approx 2^{128}$, adversarial query bound $q\approx 2^{64}$, simulator query bound $q_{\mathrm{sim}}\approx 2^{64}$, distinguishing advantage $\varepsilon\ll 1$, and lifter running time $t_{\mathrm{lif}}\ll q_{\mathrm{sim}}$.

scope.domain: White-box pseudorandom-permutation security of the 256-bit-block cipher SPACE256-16.
assumptions: The lifter running time is much smaller than the simulator query bound.
parameters: ε: distinguishing advantage, much less than 1
scope.unresolved_remainder: Prove or refute that SPACE256-16 satisfies the stated whPRP security claim in this parameter regime.

citations.label: A Modular Approach to the Incompressibility of Block-Cipher-Based AEADs

progress.summary: The paper explicitly presents the parameterized whPRP claim as a conjecture. Its appendix offers heuristic security discussion rather than a proof, leaving the claim unresolved.
citation_labels: Akinori Hosoyamada et al., A Modular Approach to the Incompressibility of Block-Cipher-Based AEADs
